items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I played with him a good while, too.

ctx.x: He said, uh, I can't figure out who that is.

Joe Howard. Joe Howard? Joe Howard, yeah. You remember Joe Howard, yeah. Oh, yeah. Uh, then he stopped, he stopped playing, and went to play bass, tuba, yeah. Mm-hmm. I played with him a good while, too. Uh, and, uh, he said, yeah, he got too old for his trumpet, so he got on, uh, bass, tuba, you know. And he used to teach, too. He was a good musician. Yes, indeed. And, uh, this son, this son Johnson, you know him?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Yeah, I went with Joe Howard's band, but I didn't stay with him long, you know.

ctx.x: Well, I asked him who he played with right before he played with Jack.

He said, who you played with before you played with Jack? Let's see. What's that with Jack? I had a kind of a big role in Robichaud's, John Robichaud's band. So that means- And then, you know, John Robichaud had a Spanish band, good, you know. And he used to play for all the rich white people. And now and then he would play for the college when they had a tag. And so, he kind of went down during the length. So his drummer, I was playing with his drummer. There was four or five piece band, Walter Blunder. You got…
Big George Williams. Yeah. I hear him in the street with Big George.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: Like Lewis DeMille, Joe Howard, and uh, uh, uh, Charles Williams, and uh, Perron. All them fellas used to see how I could read it. They'd just help me out.

ctx.x: He said who was it couldn't read?

Named Pinn? Pinn, Pinn and uh. Oh Pinn? Pinn. Pinn. Pinn he couldn't read. He couldn't read or Lee. Yeah. Zeb kept by telling Buddy to read. Lee could spell a little bit Lee Cotty but maybe Lee was something like me you know. I always kept with musicians and learning more with him and learning under there. And that's where I was. I was taking about four or five lessons with different teachers you know. I'd tell about, that'd take about five or six months. You know a lesson. But all I'd learn from them fellas…
Did Buddy and Louis Armstrong ever buck? No.
